course_description:
In the past, ore fragmentation, comminution, processing, and concentration were viewed as isolated activities, each optimised separately. Today, the approach has evolved significantly, with every process integrated into the overall recovery effort. This course introduces key concepts of the mineral extraction value chain, placing a strong emphasis on the initial comminution stage (i.e. drilling and blasting) and its influence on subsequent downstream activities. Additionally, the course will introduce practical tools and processes used to implement integrated optimisation strategies, such as “mine to mill' and value-based ore control.

This course provides the foundation for understanding the key stages of the value chain, focussing on skills to optimise mining extraction processes by the implementation of leading practices in blast design, analysis and continuous improvement. The course will include the following aspects:

course_aims: This course aims to equip the student with knowledge and understanding of the impact of all stages of the rock fragmentation and comminution processes;ﾠ but in particular the leverage of the drilling and blasting on the overall value chain. The course will introduce concepts and practical tools to help design and implement integrated mine process optimisation strategies.

learning_outcomes.description: Examine and evaluate the fundamental concepts of the mining process value chain, including ore fragmentation and mineral liberation principles.
Analyse the influence of geotechnical and geometallurgical data on fragmentation outcomes and final recovery across the stages of rock blasting, crushing and grinding.
Evaluate the key components of blasting engineering design, including objective setting, blast domain characterisation, drilling system selection, and explosive selection criteria.
Assess the relationship between explosive properties, detonation performance, rock mass damage mechanisms, and resultant fragmentation outcomes.

Apply analytical and empirical models to predict and evaluate blasting outcomes, including rock mass damage, fragmentation distribution, muckpile characteristics, ground vibration, and air blast overpressure.
Evaluate downstream process modelling requirements and design alternatives to achieve specific targets, incorporating socio-environmental considerations, and continuous improvement strategies.
Design and implement mine-to-mill optimisation strategies, using collaborative approaches to address complex operational challenges.
Evaluate design implementation procedures, safety protocols, and regulatory requirements, ensuring compliance with industry standards and best practices.
Work professionally and equitably as a group to analyse blast design alternatives using technical concepts and recommend an optimal design solution.

learning_activities.topic: Live online course introduction session and Q&A Online session which will provide an overview of the course structure, including online modules and Problem-Based Learning (PBL) activities. The session will outline assessment requirements and overall expectations. It will also introduce current and emerging challenges in mining, with a focus on the importance of fragmentation through drill and blast within the mining value chain. The aim is to set the scene, followed by discussion and a Q&A session. The Week 1 date, time, and meeting link are provided in Blackboard. Learning outcomes: L01

The Mining Value Chain Complete the online module and quiz before the scheduled problem based learning activity. This module provides a brief description of theory of constraints and how it relates to mine process optimisation. This module also provides practical examples of the mining value chain and the impact of drill and blast on downstream activities. Learning outcomes: L01, L02
On campus PBL session 1 On campus PBL activity associated with the impact of blasting on downstream activities. Learning outcomes: L01, L02

Rock blasting fundamentals Complete the online module and quiz before the PBL activity. This module covers an introduction to explosive rock interaction, breakage and explosive performance. It also concludes with a brief description of the different types of blasting activities implemented in the mining industry. Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04
On campus PBL session 2 This PBL activity focuses on various blast types, the key characteristics of explosive charges, and methods for quantifying their performance. Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04

The D&B tool kit Complete the online module and quiz before the PBL activity. This module covers the type of drilling, explosives and initiation systems used in mining activities. Learning outcomes: L03, L05, L08

On campus PBL session 3 On campus PBL activity - Blasthole diameter and drilling rig selection. Estimate performance based on rock mass properties and explore explosive selection guidelines. Learning outcomes: L03, L05, L08

Practical blast damage and fragmentation modelling Complete the online module and quiz before the PBL activity. These modules describe damage and fragmentation models used in industry to support design and optimisation processes. Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04, L05
On campus PBL session 4 On campus PBL activity focussing on the application of practical blast damage and fragmentation models. Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04, L05

Open pit blast design and analysis Complete the online module and quiz before the PBL activity. This module focuses on the blast design process as applied to open pit blasting with particular emphasis on metalliferous operations. Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04, L05, L06
On campus PBL session 5 On-campus PBL activity - an open pit blast design exercise using the JKSIMBLAST 2D Bench software platform for design and analysis. Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04, L05, L06

Underground development blasting Complete the online module and quiz before PBL activity. This module covers the design techniques applied in horizontal development blasting. Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L04, L05
On campus PBL session 6 On campus PBL activity - Underground development blast design activity with the application of JKSIMBLAST 2DFace. Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L04, L05

Underground production blasting Complete the online module and associated quiz prior to the PBL activity. The module adopts a practical approach to the design and implementation of underground production blasts, with a primary focus on uphole and downhole ring designs across a range of underground mining methods. Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L04, L05
On campus PBL session 7 On campus PBL activity - Underground production blasting activity that involves the application of the JKMSIMBLAST 2DRing software. Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L04, L05

Environmental impacts of blasting with a focus on surface mining Complete the online module and quiz before the PBL activity. This module provides a brief description of the environmental impacts of blasting and how they can be managed. Learning outcomes: L03, L05, L08

On campus PBL session 8 On-campus PBL activity focused on understanding the main environmental impacts of blasting and applying tools to manage these impacts, including far-field vibration, fumes, and flyrock. Learning outcomes: L03, L05, L08

Introduction to Mineral Processing Complete the online module and Quiz. This module provides an introduction to mineral processing focussing on crushing and grinding circuits for metal extraction. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06, L07
Group project progress update On campus progress update presentations and feedback prior to final submission of group project report. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06, L07, L09

Mine process optimisation strategies focusing on Mine to Mill Complete the online module and associated quiz prior to the PBL activity. This module outlines strategies that have been successfully implemented to optimise mineral extraction in open-pit operations, with particular emphasis on Mine-to-Mill and ore control approaches. Completion of the introductory mineral processing module in Week 10 is recommended to ensure a clear understanding of the optimisation strategies presented. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06, L07
On campus PBL session 9 On campus PBL activity - Introduction to mineral processing and the application of Mine to Mill modelling and simulations strategies. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06, L07

Design implementation and operational considerations Complete online module and Quiz. This module focuses on operational and design implementation processes, regulatory matters including standard operating procedures, safety and security. Learning outcomes: L06, L08

On campus PBL session 10 and group project working session On-campus PBL activity introducing standard operating procedures to reinforce operational concepts, safety, and practical design implementation. The session will also provide time for groups to work on their drill and blast (D&B) design and optimisation project. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06, L07, L08, L09

Revision, discussions and Q&A The final session provides a revision of key course concepts, integrating material from online modules and PBL activities. It aims to reinforce understanding of core principles. The session concludes with an open Q&A, offering students the opportunity to clarify concepts, discuss challenges, and consolidate their learning in preparation for the final exam. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06, L07, L08
